newsitem.title: USA: Ride buys part of C.A.S. Sports unit.
newsitem.headline: Ride buys part of C.A.S. Sports unit.

text.p: Ride Inc said it closed the sale of a portion of its C.A.S. Sports International Inc unit to a newly-formed corporation controlled by James Salter and Kenneth Finkelstein and owned in part by C.A.S. employees.
In connection with the deal, Salter and Finkelstein have resigned from Ride's board of directors.
In late September, a group of potential purchasers led by Chris Staff were unable to raise the necessary financing to complete the acquisition announced by Ride on September 11.
At that time, Ride began negotiating with the Salter- and Finkelstein-led purchasing group.

The sale included C.A.S.'s business segments of buying excess snowboard and sporting goods inventories from manufacturers and selling them to retailers and the sale of snowboards and related products on an original equipment manufacturer basis to other snowboard companies.

The segments were sold for $3 million, resulting in an immediate pre-tax gain on the sale of about $500,000 for Ride. The $3 million sales price is to be paid $1 million in cash and the remaining $2 million in long-term promissory notes bearing interest at the prime rate. The long-term notes are secured by a pledge of all of C.A.S.'s common stock.
In addition, the purchaser will purchase C.A.S.'s existing inventory for its net book value, estimated at $1 million.

The excess inventory sales and brokered OEM segments of C.A.S. together generated about $13 million in revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 1996, and were expected to produce approximately $13 million in 1997 revenues under Ride ownership.
